"''Yeah. He had a wife and daughter. Yeager never talks about them.|Marcus Speedstar and Kazuda Xiono talk about Jarek Yeager's family, including his daughter|audio=YeagersDaughter-ThePlatformClassic.flac|}} A [[human]] [[Gender|female]] was the '''daughter''' of the [[racer]] [[Jarek Yeager]] and his [[Jarek Yeager's wife|wife]]. The [[Yeager family|daughter]] was [[Death|killed]] around [[20 ABY]], along with their [[Parent|mother]], in an accident during a racing event in which their father raced alongside his brother, [[Marcus Speedstar]]. Speedstar would crash his [[racing starfighter]] after recklessly spiking [[Galaxy's Glory|his racer]] with [[coaxium]] hyperfuel, resulting in the deaths of the daughter and her mother. Yeager held his brother responsible for the fate of his family, and the resulting feud between them lasted for many [[Standard year|years]], until Speedstar tracked down Yeager on the ''[[Colossus]]'' [[Trantor-class supertanker fuel depot|refueling station]] on the [[planet]] [[Castilon]] in [[34 ABY]], and Yeager accepted his apology. ==Biography== ===Early life=== {{Quote|Yeager had a family.|Kazuda Xiono discovers the photograph of Yeager with his daughter|audio=YeagersFamily-FuelForTheFire.flac|}} [[File:YeagerFamily-FuelForTheFire.png|thumb|left|215px|Jarek Yeager's daughter with their parents on Batuu]] A [[human]] [[Gender|female]] was the daughter of the [[racer]] [[Jarek Yeager]] and his [[Jarek Yeager's wife|wife]]. At some point, the daughter was photographed with both [[parent]]s on the [[planet]]''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' [[Batuu]].{{SW|url=news/buckets-list-extra-fuel-for-the-fire-star-wars-resistance|text=Bucket's List Extra: 10 Fun Facts from "Fuel for the Fire" - ''Star Wars Resistance''}} Yeager, a former [[New Republic pilot|pilot]] in the [[New Republic Defense Fleet]], left the [[New Republic Defense Force|military]] following its [[Military Disarmament Act|downsizing]] and became a racer to earn a living for his [[Marriage|wife]] and daughter. Around [[20 ABY]], the [[Yeager family|family]] attended a race that both Yeager and his brother [[Marcus Speedstar]] were participating in. In an attempt to beat his older brother, Speedstar used heavy amounts of volatile [[coaxium]] to fuel [[Galaxy's Glory|his racer]]. During the race, the coaxium-fueled [[Racing starfighter|ship]] combusted and crashed, [[Death|killing]] Yeager's daughter and wife in the process. The incident led to Yeager and Speedstar becoming estranged for over ten [[Standard year|years]]; Yeager held Speedstar responsible for the accident, and Speedstar initially refused to apologize. ===Legacy=== {{Quote|You might not have realized it, but he thinks of you like a daughter, Tam. Losing one was painful enough.|Venisa Doza tells Tamara Ryvora about Yeager's caring for her|audio=YeagersDaughter-RendezvousPoint.flac|{{Resistance|Rendezvous Point (episode)}}}} Yeager kept the photograph of his family on Batuu in his [[Jarek Yeager's Repair Station|repair station]] onboard the ''[[Colossus]]'' [[Trantor-class supertanker fuel depot|refueling station]] on the planet [[Castilon]]. During his time on the ''Colossus'', Yeager came to care for the [[Technician|mechanic]] [[Tamara Ryvora]], who was part of his [[Team Fireball|team]], and came to think of her almost like a daughter. After sneaking into Yeager's station in [[34 ABY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' places the events of [[Star Wars Resistance Season One|''Star Wars Resistance'' Season One]], which includes the episodes "[[Fuel for the Fire]]" and "[[The Platform Classic]]", in [[34 ABY]]. the [[Resistance]] [[Spy|operative]] [[Kazuda Xiono]], who was working for Yeager, discovered the photo of Yeager with his wife and daughter. Xiono was interested by the photo, as he had not known about Yeager's family. [[File:MarcusSpeedstar-ThePlatformClassic.jpg|thumb|right|170px|Speedstar hoped to apologize to Yeager for the incident.]] Later that year, Speedstar arrived on the ''Colossus'' to participate in the [[Platform Classic]] race. While there, he attempted to reconnect with his brother, but Yeager continued to shun him, having not forgiven him for his role in his daughter's death. After witnessing the siblings' feud, Xiono spoke with Speedstar and learned about the tragedy. During the Platform Classic—which Yeager also entered to compete against his brother—Speedstar admitted he had been too ashamed to apologize following the accident and pleaded with Yeager to forgive him, telling his brother he had been searching for him and wanted the chance to apologize. Yeager accepted the apology, and after the race, the two brothers hugged: when Speedstar asked if they were good, Yeager stated that they would be one day soon. Later that year,{{ResistanceDate|2|8}} Yeager's former colleague, the [[Resistance pilot|pilot]] [[Venisa Doza]], was captured by the [[First Order]]. During her time aboard the [[Resurgent-class Star Destroyer|Star Destroyer]] ''[[Thunderer]]'', Doza met Ryvora, who had since left the ''Colossus'' to become a [[First Order TIE fighter pilot|First Order pilot]] following a falling-out with Yeager. While [[Escape of Venisa Doza|escaping]] the ''Thunderer'' and using Ryvora as a hostage, Doza learned of the First Order [[pilot]]'s circumstances, informing her that even if she did not realize it, Yeager missed her and thought of her like a daughter. The Resistance pilot added that Yeager was in enough pain from losing his real daughter. ==Personality and traits== Yeager's daughter had dark skin, [[Color|black]] [[hair]], and brown [[eye]]s. ==Equipment== During the family's trip to Batuu, the daughter [[Clothing|wore]] yellow overalls, white shoes, a white top, and silver [[bracelet]]s on both [[Limb|arms]]. ==Behind the scenes== ===Development=== {{Quote|I think that Yeager sort of, essentially […] almost adopted her in a way like, ''[sic]'' you know really became this father figure, and I think that his concern in terms of his family and just, you know, how dangerous racing is, I think he sort of intentionally kind of kept her grounded out of fear.|Brandon Auman describes Yeager's relationship to Tam Ryvora and how his daughter's fate impacted it|audio=YeagersDaughter-BrandonAuman.flac|{{WookYouTube|ML1nYpSU0d0|Wookieepedia Interviews - Brandon Auman}}}} Jarek Yeager's daughter first appeared in a photograph in "[[Fuel for the Fire]]," the fourth episode of the [[Star Wars Resistance Season One|first season]] of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars Resistance]]'', which aired on [[October 21]], [[2018]].{{DisneyPress|wdtv=1|url=disneychannel/shows/star-wars-resistance/episodes|text=Star Wars Resistance}} The photo of the family was created by artist [[Kilian Plunkett]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.kilianplunkett.com/star-wars-resistance|text=Star Wars - Resistance|work=[[Kilian Plunkett]]'s [https://www.kilianplunkett.com official website]|archivedate=20241107032212}} [[File:TeamFireball-ThePlatformClassic.png|thumb|left|320px|Yeager's backstory was fleshed out in "The Platform Classic."]] Although the daughter's existence was revealed in "Fuel for the Fire," the story of the family was not divulged until later in the episode "[[The Platform Classic]],"{{WookYouTube|video=c-i_MhMIFnA|text=Wookieepedia Interviews - Doc Wyatt & Chris Burke}} the first season's ninth episode, which aired on [[November 25]], 2018. [[Kevin Burke]], one of the two writers for the episode, felt that the heart of the episode, as well as the character of Yeager at large, was about handling regret, overcoming loss, and dealing with personal darkness, all of which the audience experiences through his stoic and guarded perspective. Burke noted that ''[[Star Wars]]'' stories overall are best at deeply exploring characters, something that often goes beyond what viewers initially think. ''Resistance'' head writer and executive producer [[Brandon Auman]] spoke about how Yeager's family impacted the relationships with his found family on the ''Colossus''. He declared that Yeager was more protective of those he cared about due to the loss of his family, including his daughter. Auman felt that Yeager took on the role of a father figure for Ryvora, something "[[Rendezvous Point (episode)|Rendezvous Point]]"—the eighth episode of [[Star Wars Resistance Season Two|Season Two]], which aired on [[November 24]], [[2019]]—acknowledges, and believed that Yeager was hesitant to let her fly due to knowing the risks associated with racing. ===Cast commentary=== {{Quote|… if there's one takeaway from the episode it's that, do you know what I mean. It's an episode about regret and overcoming loss, and that's very much the heart of it and the heart of this character.|Kevin Burke|audio=YeagersDaughter-KevinBurke.flac|}} [[File:Jarek.jpg|thumb|right|185px|The show's cast agreed that Jarek Yeager's family backstory was hugely important.]] In the episode commentary for "The Platform Classic" included in the [[Star Wars Resistance: Complete Season One|DVD compilation]] of Season One, voice actors [[Christopher Sean]], who portrays Xiono; [[Josh Brener]], who portrays [[Neeku Vozo]]; [[Scott Lawrence]], who portrays Yeager; and [[Myrna Velasco]], who portrays [[Torra Doza]], discussed their thoughts on Yeager's backstory involving his wife and daughter. Brener noted that Yeager, a private and closed-off character, having his life story being told to everyone was a dramatic struggle for him. Sean felt that it was one of his favorite storylines in the show and recalled being emotionally moved by the episode. Lawrence agreed, saying that it was one of the heavier topics in the show's first season, which Sean furthered by adding that the narrative helped explain why Yeager was on the ''Colossus''.{{HomeVideoCite|set=Star Wars Resistance: Complete Season One|episode=The Platform Classic}} As Burke noted, Yeager's rich backstory is what makes viewers truly appreciate him, something that Sean also pointed out. Sean and Velasco spoke on the scene where Yeager partly accepts Speedstar's apology and connected with Yeager's stance of appreciating the gesture but admitting that he needed more time for them to be "good." Sean felt that the honesty in Yeager's words was important, while Velasco pointed to Yeager still being willing to thank Speedstar for the gesture as being equally valuable. They asserted that the situation of being angry at someone who needs your help is a relatable struggle for viewers. Overall, the cast agreed that the episode emphasized the importance of family togetherness and love, one of the main themes of the show. ==Appearances== *{{Resistance|Fuel for the Fire}} {{1st}} {{C|Appears in photograph}} *{{ResistanceAnimationCite|4|Fuel for the Fire (comic story)}} {{C|Appears in photograph}} *{{Resistance|The Platform Classic}} {{Mo}} *{{Resistance|Rendezvous Point (episode)}} {{Mo}} ==Sources== *{{SW|url=news/buckets-list-extra-fuel-for-the-fire-star-wars-resistance|text=Bucket's List Extra: 10 Fun Facts from "Fuel for the Fire" - ''Star Wars Resistance''}} *{{SWYouTube|series=Resistance Rewind|text=#1.4: Who is Yeager?|video=oUBjuDXEG3A|sw_url=video/yeager-s-story-resistance-rewind}} *''[[Star Wars Resistance: Complete Season One]]'' *''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' {{Imo}} *''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' *{{Databank|jarek-yeager|Jarek Yeager}} {{Imo}} *{{Databank|yeager-s-garage|Yeager's garage}} ==Notes and references== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Jarek Yeager's daughter}} {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |fr=Fille de Jarek Yeager |ka=ჯარეკ იეგერის ქალიშვილი }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yeager, Jarek's daughter}} [[Category:Females]] [[Category:Humans]] [[Category:Individuals with unspecified pronouns]]
